platformConstraints: Lynx CSS has no :hover, @media or pseudo-elements: states are tap states, the case is one fluid column.
Theme variables live on page, not :root, as rgba() values (a hex with a digit-e-digit run is mangled by the CSS pipeline).
A background-image url() in styles.css draws nothing on iOS; the brushed-brass and mahogany rasters are bound inline from case/materials.ts, and the classes keep the bevels and fallback colors.
SVG is rendered from strings by <svg content> and cannot read CSS variables: the dial, index, plan and chevrons carry literal hex copies of the tokens.
Text does not inherit fonts: every <text> names its family. Bodoni Moda is shipped as static instances because Lynx picks no variable-font axes.
Lynx Explorer has no <canvas>: the orrery is drawn as a flat SVG plan with a note saying why.

narrative.overview:
The app is the machine itself: an 18th-century brass orrery standing in a dark room, its arms carrying each planet to where it really is on the date shown, and below it the mahogany case that holds its controls. The top of the screen is the machine in 3D, full bleed over a night sky; the bottom is the case, separated from it by a brass edge, holding a brass date dial seen through a slot, a silvered window engraved with the date, and either two whole rows of brass name plates with the maker's cartouche, or, flown in to a body, a silvered specification plate. Flying in, the brass and the orbits fall away and the model becomes the real world.

The world is a material law before it is a palette: brass is what moves or can be touched, silver carries every figure, black wax fills every engraving, mahogany holds it all. Color lives in the planets (real NASA/USGS maps and live GLSL); the case stays in its metals and wood. It is dark whatever the phone's setting, because it's a machine in a room at night.

It refuses the dark space explorer with glowing cyan HUD and frosted glass cards.
keyCharacteristics: Three metals and a wood, each with one job: brass moves, silver tells, wax engraves, mahogany holds.
One engraved serif in three cuts, caps widely tracked for everything cut into metal; a copperplate script for the cartouche alone.
Depth by bevels: 1px lit-over-shade rules on brass and silver, never drop shadows.
Real materials: brushed brass and mahogany grain are procedural rasters bound inline; silvered plate is a smooth gradient.
One green, verdigris, and only on the dial's index when it shows today.

rules.name: The Metals By Law Rule
rules.body: Brass moves (anything you drag or tap), silver tells (every figure), mahogany holds. No metal does another's job: a figure is never set on brass, a control is never silver.

rules.name: The Color Lives In The Planets Rule
rules.body: The case stays in its metals and wood. The only hue outside them is verdigris on today's index; planet colors appear only on the planets themselves (and the plan's discs).

rules.name: The Always Night Rule
rules.body: The app does not follow light mode.

rules.name: The One Hand Rule
rules.body: Copperplate script is the maker's signature and appears once, in the cartouche. Everything else is engraved Bodoni.

rules.name: The Name Every Text Rule
rules.body: Lynx text doesn't inherit fonts: every `<text>` names its family (`font-engraved`, `font-display`, `font-italic`, `font-script`).

rules.name: The Bevel Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: Raised and sunk are 1px lit and shade borders on the metal's own color. Never a drop shadow on a flat fill.

rules.name: The Whole Units Rule
rules.body: Plates sit in whole rows; nothing in the case is clipped or scrolled.

rules.name: The Double Rule Rule
rules.body: Orbits are single engraved hairlines; the chosen planet's orbit becomes a double rule, never a brighter or thicker line.

dos: **Do** make every touchable thing brass with the brushed raster bound inline from `case/materials.ts`, and every stated figure silver.
**Do** bevel metal with 1px lit and shade borders; brass raised, silver set in, pressed brass inverted.
**Do** engrave text in wax with the 1px lit lip, caps tracked 1-3px for names and labels.
**Do** give literal SVG strokes and fills the hex of the matching token, since SVG can't read CSS variables.
**Do** keep plates in whole rows and the case's well a fixed height.
**Do** honor reduced motion: cut the flight, stop idle drift.
donts: **Don't** put a drop shadow on brass or silver, or any shadow on a flat fill.
**Don't** use verdigris anywhere but today's index, or bring any other hue into the case.
**Don't** use the copperplate script for anything but the cartouche.
**Don't** brighten or thicken an orbit to select it; double it.
**Don't** write a `url()` raster in styles.css; it doesn't draw on iOS.
**Don't** add a light theme, glowing HUD lines or frosted glass cards.
